title: Nevermind
wiki_lead:
Nevermind is the second studio album by American rock band Nirvana, released on September 24, 1991, by DGC Records. Produced by Butch Vig, Nevermind features a more polished, radio-friendly sound than the band's prior work. It was recorded at Sound City Studios in Van Nuys, California, and Smart Studios in Madison, Wisconsin, in May and June 1991, and mastered that August at the Mastering Lab in Hollywood, California. Nevermind was Nirvana's first album to feature drummer Dave Grohl.
Written primarily by frontman Kurt Cobain, the album's lyrical themes include social alienation and frustration, anti-establishment and feminist views, and relationship issues; these were more sensitive compared to what was common in mainstream rock music at the time. Musically rooted in grunge and alternative rock, the album also features acoustic ballads and punk-inspired hard rock. 
Nevermind was an unexpected success, topping the Billboard 200 in January 1992. The lead single, "Smells Like Teen Spirit", reached the Top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100 and was later inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame. The singles "Come as You Are", "Lithium", and "In Bloom" were also successful. Nevermind was voted the best album of the year in Pazz & Jop critics' poll, while "Smells Like Teen Spirit" also topped the single-of-the-year and video-of-the-year polls. It was nominated for three Grammy Awards, including Best Alternative Music Album.
Nevermind brought Nirvana worldwide fame, with Cobain dubbed by many as the "voice of his generation". The album is generally credited with bringing grunge and alternative rock to a mainstream audience, accelerating the decline of hair metal, and initiating a resurgence of punk culture among the youth of Generation X. Nevermind has sold more than 30 million copies worldwide, making it one of the best-selling albums of all time. In 2024, it was certified 13× platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America. Nevermind was added by the Library of Congress to the National Recording Registry in 2004 as "culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant", and frequently appears on lists of the greatest albums.

Background and early sessions
In early 1990, Nirvana began planning their second album for their record company Sub Pop, tentatively titled Sheep. At the suggestion of Sub Pop head Bruce Pavitt, Nirvana selected Butch Vig as producer. The band particularly liked Vig's work with Killdozer. They traveled to Vig's Smart Studios in Madison, Wisconsin, and recorded from April 2 to 6, 1990. Most of the basic arrangements were complete, but songwriter Kurt Cobain was still working on lyrics and the band was unsure of which songs to record. Ultimately, eight were recorded, some of which were later rerecorded for Nevermind: "Imodium" (later renamed "Breed"), "Dive" (later released as the B-side to "Sliver"), "In Bloom", "Pay to Play" (later renamed "Stay Away"), "Sappy", "Lithium", "Here She Comes Now" (released on Heaven & Hell: A Tri
grok_lead: Nevermind is the second studio album and major-label debut by the American rock band Nirvana, released on September 24, 1991, by DGC Records. Produced primarily by Butch Vig, it marked the first Nirvana album to feature drummer Dave Grohl and included the breakout single " Smells Like Teen Spirit," whose raw energy and satirical lyrics captured widespread youth disillusionment. The record's polished yet abrasive sound blended punk influences with heavy riffing, propelling the Seattle grunge scene from underground obscurity to global commercial dominance and displacing prevailing hair metal trends. Despite initial modest sales expectations of around 50,000 copies, Nevermind surged to number one on the Billboard 200 after "Smells Like Teen Spirit" topped modern rock charts, eventually selling over 30 million copies worldwide and earning 13Ã platinum certification from the RIAA in the United States as of December 2024. Its success facilitated broader exposure for grunge acts like Soundgarden and Pearl Jam, reshaping rock music's mainstream landscape toward authenticity over artifice, though it also intensified internal band tensions amid Kurt Cobain's rising fame and substance issues. The album's iconic cover photograph, showing a naked infant Spencer Elden swimming toward a dollar bill on a fishhook, symbolized consumerist corruption of innocence but later drew controversy, including lawsuits by Elden alleging child sexual exploitation through its distribution; federal courts dismissed these claims multiple times, most recently in October 2025, citing lack of harm and the image's artistic intent. While praised for democratizing alternative rock, Nevermind faced critique for commodifying subcultural rebellion, with Cobain himself expressing ambivalence over its polished production and unforeseen ubiquity.
